newsitem.title: UK: UK ex-premier Heath finds publisher for memoirs.
newsitem.headline: UK ex-premier Heath finds publisher for memoirs.

text.p: Former prime minister Edward Heath, who took Britain into Europe, is to publish his memoirs in October 1998, his publishers announced on Tuesday.

Heath, 81, will describe his early life, student days at Oxford and his World War Two army career before moving on to his entry into the House of Commons in 1950, publishers Hodder and Stoughton said.
The ex-premier will then chronicle his election to the leadership of the Conservative Party in 1965 and his time as prime minister from 1970-74.

"This is not just the autobiography of one of our leading statesmen, but a uniquely revealing account of the panoply of post-war 20th century political and social history," said Hodder chief executive Tim Hely Hutchinson.

Heath has been promising to publish his memoirs for more than 20 years. He was signed up by another publishing company in the 1980s but eventually returned his 50,000 pounds ($82,000) advance in the early 1990s.
Heath will no doubt be looking to outsell the woman who succeeded him as party leader and who he came to regard with implacable hostility -- Margaret Thatcher.
Many thousands of copies of her second volume of autobigraphy remain unsold and publishing experts warn that political memoirs must be amusing and, if possible, spicy, to sell well.

Apart from his political career, Heath made a name for himself in the worlds of music -- he is an accomplished conductor -- and yacht racing, publishing popular books on the subjects. ($ = 0.608 British Pounds)
